title: AI;DR (AI; Didn't Read)
author: mooreds
relevanceReason: 命中 2 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: I’m SUPER jealous that I didn’t think of this first...Alas! Hat tip to seclilc for tweeting this gem out two days ago.lil c@seclilcAI;DR

(AI; didn’t read)4:13 PM · Aug 15, 2026 · 346K Views83 Replies · 2.09K Reposts · 16.6K LikesI’ve been thinking about it ever since. Why? Because there is growing grumbling among everyone about AI writing. And it’s not just others; it’s me! I am getting to the point where I physically flinch (sometimes dropping my shoulders and hunching, or having a slight eye twitch) when someone I respect sends me unfiltered and unedited AI output.Look, I get it. It’s Q3 2026, and we should expect that everyone is utilizing AI at SOME point in their process (sourcing ideas, creating outlines, refining prose, etc.).However, I have a new policy.If you’re not bothered enough to review and edit it......then I’m not going to bother reading it.Yes, there are certain situations in which we should expect 100% AI-generated copy. Customer support would be a perfect example. We’re not looking for artisanal “did you make sure to reset your phone” style dialogue.But if you’re my colleague and we’re in a Slack discussion and you post a wall of Claude output, then I’m afraid I received a different message than you intended.The same is true for people’s newsletters and social content. It’s your name on it; are you proud of the prose and weird AI-isms sprinkled throughout it? If so, great. But I can ask Claude directly if I wanted to.TL;DR (too long; didn’t read) was the solution for social media.AI;DR (AI; didn’t read) is the solution for AI slop.May you embrace this policy yourself and seek out those willing to care enough to prioritize a human touch when they talk to you.No posts

comments.author: LPisGood
comments.textRawHtml:
My coworkers continue to dump hundreds of lines of AI documentation in every PR and every other line of code has between one and ten lines of AI generated comments, talking about the real unlock and how things are byte for byte identical on the load bearing path or how the acceptance ladder is misleading.

Features are coming out and metrics are improving, but we’re basically in a post readability code base, with the occasional performative comment about a variable name.

I don’t really know how to address this situation or if it needs addressed. I certainly don’t read the long-winded AI comments or the AI documentation, but perhaps it’s useful for the AI on its next pass.
comments.textZhHtml:
我的同事们继续在每个 PR 中转储数百行 AI 文档，并且每隔一行代码都有一到十行 AI 生成的注释，谈论真正的解锁以及负载路径上的内容如何逐字节相同或接受阶梯如何误导。

功能正在出现，指标正在改进，但我们基本上处于后期可读性代码库中，偶尔会对变量名称进行执行评论。

I真的不知道如何解决这种情况或者是否需要解决。我当然不会阅读冗长的 AI 评论或 AI 文档，但也许它对 AI 的下一次迭代很有用。

children.author: aaaronic
children.textRawHtml: My "favorite" Claudism is when I critique its work and ask it to remove some unnecessary part of the design -- and then the diff has more green than red because it added comments about why the code is no longer there -- the code that was never in the mainline and never asked for!
children.textZhHtml: 我“最喜欢”的克劳主义是当我批评它的工作并要求它删除一些不必要的设计部分时——然后差异的绿色多于红色，因为它添加了关于为什么代码不再存在的注释——这些代码从未出现在主线中，也从未被要求！

children.author: roarcher
children.textRawHtml: Oh god this has been driving me nuts since Opus 5 landed. Every docblock is filled with long-winded jargon explaining why this design is superior to some other design, which never existed as far as any dev who might read that comment is concerned.
children.textZhHtml: 天哪，自从 Opus 5 发布以来，这一直让我发疯。每个文档块都充满了冗长的行话，解释为什么这种设计优于其他一些设计，而对于任何可能阅读该评论的开发人员来说，其他设计从未存在过。

children.author: tehlike
children.textRawHtml:
This has been a thing for long while, on codex too.

You ask it to do something, then tell it to do something in a different way, then it assumes it needs to do the refactor in a backward compatible way, or creates migrations for it etc.
children.textZhHtml:
这件事已经存在很长时间了，在 Codex 上也是如此。

你要求它做某事，然后告诉它以不同的方式做某事，然后它假设它需要以向后兼容的方式进行重构，或者为其创建迁移等。

children.author: geysersam
children.textRawHtml: Omg the "backwards compatible fix" in a one-off script, I feel my ptsd coming on ...
children.textZhHtml: 天哪，一次性脚本中的“向后兼容修复”，我感觉我的 ptsd 即将到来......

children.author: theshrike79
children.textRawHtml:
This is why I started adding a PROJECT.md file to all my projects and a hook for claude to read it.

It contains (Among other things) stuff like "this is a single user personal project, I'm the only user, this will never be open to the public internet" etc.

It kinda-sorta tones down the proclivity to worry about backwards compatibility and slight edge cases where if someone has edited some template and the new code doesn't support it.
children.textZhHtml:
这就是为什么我开始在我的所有项目中添加一个 PROJECT.md 文件以及一个供 claude 阅读的钩子。

它包含（除其他外）诸如“这是一个单用户个人项目，我是唯一的用户，这永远不会向公共互联网开放”等内容。

它有点降低了担心向后兼容性和轻微边缘情况（如果有人编辑了某些模板）的倾向。并且新代码不支持它。

children.author: stelonix
children.textRawHtml:
Oh good I thought I was doing something wrong! Using ChatGPT web for planning, ask for a prompt then notice something weird in the prompt and whether I:

1) use the edit in-place functionality; or

2) ask it to rewrite to remove something

It'll write the prompt as if the agent (codex) knew about the conversation and add "don't do X" etc. At first that bothered but I realized it doesn't really change the output so I stopped caring.

Still, no experience is unique I guess.
children.textZhHtml:
哦，太好了，我以为我做错了什么！使用 ChatGPT Web 进行规划，询问提示，然后注意提示中的一些奇怪的内容以及我是否：

1) 使用就地编辑功能；或者

2）要求它重写以删除某些内容

它会编写提示，就好像代理（codex）知道对话一样，并添加“不要做X”等。起初这很麻烦，但我意识到它并没有真正改变输出，所以我不再关心。

不过，我想没有什么经验是独一无二的。

children.author: Uptrenda
children.textRawHtml: I remember when I was updating some formats for my apps data files and it ended up writing v2 and laying it on top of the old one. Ended up just telling it to delete the entire feature and start again. I do think claude.md instructions help though.
children.textZhHtml: 我记得当我更新应用程序数据文件的某些格式时，最终编写了 v2 并将其放在旧版本之上。最后只是告诉它删除整个功能并重新开始。我确实认为 claude.md 说明有帮助。

children.author: tehlike
children.textRawHtml: They do. But you need to remember.
children.textZhHtml: 他们确实如此。但你需要记住。

children.author: foolserrandboy
children.textRawHtml: Oh no, you said "landed"! It's dug into our brains!
children.textZhHtml: 哦不，你说的是“着陆”！它已经深入我们的大脑！

children.author: doix
children.textRawHtml:
I hate that I have to change the way I write to avoid AI-isms. I loved using "load bearing" to describe weird code that you think you can delete but is actually holding everything together.

Now people think I'm just parroting what Claude said. It sucks. I want my catch phrases back, I guess this is how em dash users felt
children.textZhHtml:
我讨厌我必须改变我的写作方式以避免人工智能主义。我喜欢用“承载”来描述奇怪的代码，你认为你可以删除这些代码，但实际上它把所有东西都组合在一起。

现在人们认为我只是在重复 Claude 所说的话。太糟糕了。我想要回我的口号，我想这就是 em dash 用户的感受

children.author: roarcher
children.textRawHtml: As a former em-dash enjoyer, I indeed feel your pain.
children.textZhHtml: 作为曾经的 em-dash 享受者，我确实感受到了你的痛苦。

children.author: filterfish
children.textRawHtml: I'm with you an that one. RIP em-dash.
children.textZhHtml: 我和你在一起。 RIP em-dash。

children.author: jannyfer
children.textRawHtml: RIP. I had frequently used ALT + 0151.
children.textZhHtml: 安息吧。我经常使用 ALT + 0151。

children.author: account42
children.textRawHtml: I feel like a lot of these have been LinkedIn-isms or PR-isms long before they have been AI-isms so not much is lost.
children.textZhHtml: 我觉得其中很多早在成为 AI 主义之前就已经是 LinkedIn 主义或公关主义了，所以并没有损失太多。

children.author: roarcher
children.textRawHtml:
I used to use em-dashes for explanatory clauses--like this one, for example--when using commas would make the sentence difficult to parse due to other nearby commas.

They're only a LinkedIn-ism when used to create an unduly dramatic juxtaposition for an otherwise mundane idea. But now they set off people's AI radar when used for any reason at all.
children.textZhHtml:
我曾经在解释性从句中使用破折号，例如这个，当使用逗号时，由于附近有其他逗号，句子会变得难以解析。

当它们被用来为一个平凡的想法创建一个过度戏剧性的并置时，它们只是一种 LinkedIn 主义。但现在，无论出于何种原因使用，它们都会引发人们的人工智能雷达。

children.author: account42
children.textRawHtml: Perhaps I am biased because I find the use of em-dashes without spaces (as is common in English typesetting) to be inherently ugly so I'm not too unhappy to see their use discouraged.
children.textZhHtml: 也许我有偏见，因为我发现使用不带空格的破折号（这在英语排版中很常见）本质上是丑陋的，所以我对于看到它们的使用受到阻碍并不太不高兴。

children.author: dag11
children.textRawHtml: You could say it landed cleanly.
children.textZhHtml: 你可以说它干净利落地。

children.author: hexasquid
children.textRawHtml: Good instinct. Fair challenge. This corrects my framing. It makes your point sharp. This is a significant finding. Positively confirmed. That settles it, and it flips the picture. Honest verdict - this is not small. Let me wire it in.
children.textZhHtml: 良好的直觉。公平的挑战。这纠正了我的框架。它使你的观点变得尖锐。这是一个重大发现。得到积极证实。这样就解决了问题，并且扭转了局面。诚实的判决——这并不小。让我把它连起来。
